distinguishing_features: Compliant low-modulus polyurethane elastomer coating applied to the impeller surface rather than a hardware material/geometry upgrade or a monitoring/prediction scheme
Erosion mitigation achieved by extending particle contact time (microseconds to milliseconds) to reduce peak contact stress below the wear threshold
Strain-rate-dependent damping of impact energy via viscoelastic layer, decoupling impact velocity from surface stress
Pressure-based pass/fail test using existing telemetry to detect coating degradation via pressure-drop deviation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce material removal on the impeller surface from high-velocity hard-particle impacts without altering the pump's flow performance or requiring new sensing hardware.
parsed.viable_reason: The 1000x contact-time increase and the impact-momentum force reduction are physically overstated and internally inconsistent with a thin 2-5 mm constrained elastomer layer; erosion of compliant coatings by hard angular quartz involves cutting/gouging, and the stated peak-stress-order-of-magnitude drop is not physically defensible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Compliant elastomer/elastomeric impeller linings and coatings for slurry erosion are well-established prior art, and the contact-time-extending mechanism is a known principle, so the distinguishing mechanism itself is an obvious step to a skilled engineer.
